newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu sinks some 3 pct to 3,880/3,930 vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu sinks some 3 pct to 3,880/3,930 vs dlr.

text.p: Romania's leu currency fell around three percent to the dollar on Wednesday, with a major market-making dealer bank quoting it at 3,880/3,930 to the dollar against 3,780/3800 in early trading.

Traders said the downswing reflected a commitment by the reformist government elected last month to allow the leu, held artificially high over the past year, to find more realistic levels on the interbank market.
The leu traded at Bucharest currency shops at around 4,750 to the dollar.

Cross rates of other currencies quoted on the interbank market deliver weaker prices, in line with retail rates. Operators have used them as a backdoor for trading since March when the local market was resticted to four dealer banks.

That move and attempts to prop the leu artificially in an election year were among the reasons behind the International Monetary Fund's suspension of a three-year credit of $460 million earlier this year.
The stabilisation programme drawn up by a new reformist government includes liberalisation of the foreign exchange market.

An IMF technical mission visited Romania last week to evaluate the economy and the Fund's Managing Director Michel Camdessus is due in Bucharest this week ahead of negotiations in January on a new credit. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
